item.title: Osaka Autumn Foliage: Minoo Falls and the Momiji Trail — Guide
item.description: For autumn colour, Osakans head north to Minoo (Mino-o), a wooded valley on the edge of the city that turns brilliant with maples each November. A gentle, paved riverside trail runs about three kilometres up the gorge from Minoo Station to the Minoo Waterfall, a 33-metre fall framed by fiery leaves at the head of the valley — one of the most rewarding easy walks in the Osaka area. Along the way, shops sell the local speciality of momiji tempura, whole maple leaves battered and deep-fried into a sweet, crisp snack.

item.title: Nunobiki Falls: Four Waterfalls Minutes from Central Kobe — Guide
item.description: Nunobiki Falls is one of the most remarkable things about Kobe: a chain of four waterfalls, celebrated in classical Japanese poetry for over a thousand years and counted among the country’s finest, sitting barely fifteen minutes' walk from a Shinkansen station. A shaded stone path climbs from behind Shin-Kobe Station past the Mendaki, Ondaki, Tsuzumigadaki and Meotodaki falls, the largest dropping some 43 metres into a green pool. Keep climbing and the trail reaches a viewing plaza over the city, the Nunobiki Herb Garden and a ropeway back down.

item.title: Shiraito Falls: A Curtain of Fuji Spring Water — Guide
item.description: Shiraito Falls, near Fujinomiya at the southwestern foot of Mount Fuji, is one of Japan’s most graceful waterfalls, its name meaning ‘white threads’ after the hundreds of silky streams of water that pour over a curved, 20-metre-high and 150-metre-wide cliff face. Almost all of the water is Mount Fuji’s rain and snowmelt, filtered through the volcanic rock for decades before emerging from the cliff itself, and the falls are a component site of Fuji’s World Heritage listing, long revered as a place of worship and purification.

item.title: Shosenkyo Gorge: One of Japan's Most Beautiful Ravines — Guide
item.description: Shosenkyo Gorge, near Kofu, is often ranked among Japan’s most beautiful gorges, offering a scenic walking trail that follows a clear river past towering granite rock formations, sculpted cliffs and the striking Sengataki Waterfall at its upper end. The gorge is especially renowned for its autumn foliage, when the mix of coloured maples against the pale granite draws large crowds, and a ropeway near the top offers panoramic views extending to Mount Fuji and the Southern Alps on clear days.

item.title: Shiraito Waterfall: Fukui's 'White Thread' Cascade — Guide
item.description: Shiraito Waterfall takes its name, meaning ‘white thread’, from the way its water spreads and separates into fine, thread-like strands as it cascades down a broad rock face, a gentler and more delicate sight than a single powerful drop of water. Set within a quiet forested valley, the falls are easily accessible via a short walk from nearby parking, making them a good stop for visitors seeking a peaceful natural spot without a demanding hike.

item.title: Akiu Onsen: Sendai's Ancient Hot Spring Retreat — Guide
item.description: Akiu Onsen, ranked among Japan’s three oldest hot springs with a history stretching back some 1,500 years, sits in a wooded gorge just 30 minutes from central Sendai. Traditional ryokan inns line the Natori River, and the dramatic 55 m Akiu Great Falls thunders down nearby, framed by maple trees that blaze crimson each autumn — making this the easiest escape-to-nature option for Sendai-based travellers. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Taihaku-ku, Sendai, Miyagi Hours Day baths and falls always open (varies by inn) Admission Day bath from ~¥800; falls free Time needed 2–3 hours Best time Autumn (foliage); year-round for onsen What to See Akiu Great Falls, a dramatic 55 m cascade.

item.title: Minoo Park Guide: Waterfall, Autumn Leaves & Fried Maple Leaves
item.description: Just half an hour from central Osaka, Minoo Park (Mino-o) is the city’s favourite nature escape — a forested river valley climbing gently to the lovely 33-metre Minoo Waterfall. The paved riverside trail is easy enough for almost anyone, lined with old tea houses and shops, and in November the maples turn the whole gorge brilliant red and gold. It’s also famous for a uniquely Osaka snack: momiji tempura, real maple leaves battered and deep-fried into a sweet, crispy treat.
